decisions.reason: Correctly identifies sessions.list.getSnapshot().current returning undefined on alpha.2, resolve() returning null, and onKeyDown exiting before preventDefault. Explains both silences accurately: the guard passes because all four presence probes check service members that still exist while only a field inside the snapshot vanished, and undefined was a legitimate no-session state the code quietly ignores. Grounded in the plugin source and type excerpts; does not claim the service was removed or throws.

Maps the change from alpha.1 SessionListState.current to its absence in alpha.2 SessionListSnapshot, cites the 'navigation belongs to view owners' doc comment, and identifies the canonical replacement as uiSession.adapter.current (ObservableSnapshot<SessionBindingValue>) yielding { key, ctx, hooks, keyedHooks, props } with key replacing current and ctx replacing sessions.scope(id). Grounded in the type excerpts, not just the reference card.

Provides fenced dual-host code: feature-detects ctx.uiSession and reads adapter.current.getSnapshot() key/ctx on alpha.2, falls back to legacy sessions.list.getSnapshot().current plus sessions.scope(id) on alpha.1, from one build. inject gains uiSession; conversation resolves via scope.get('conversation') and input.for receives the binding scope. Equivalent shape accepted; guard order acceptable.

Names the breakage class as field-level removal behind service-level stability, notes the guard runs once at activation while the break recurs per keystroke, and specifies a hardened guard that feature-detects the actual capability (assert the snapshot current field on alpha-1-shaped hosts, detect uiSession.adapter.current on alpha-2-shaped hosts) running lazily or per-use rather than only at activation.

Verification includes a temporary probe of adapter.current key with one session open, chord behavior on both hosts after the fix, and typechecking against alpha.2 published types as the pre-ship gate. Prevention proposes a deprecated getter that throws/warns on read or a runtime snapshot-shape contract, turning the silent removal into a loud failure.

caps.reason: The final remedy is the current-session code fix through uiSession.adapter.current with a legacy fallback, not slot re-registration or inject re-declaration alone; inject change is correctly paired with the code change.
